Hi Sara — appreciate the clear list. Below is a practical, short-form option we commonly propose for customers running a pilot then committing to a private deployment. I attached a draft SOW and a simple pricing model for your procurement team.

Proposal (pilot -> commit):
1) Pilot (0-6 months):
   - Platform fee waived for months 1-3, 50% platform fee for months 4-6 (onramp credit of 75% value applied as monthly bill credit)
   - Implementation retainer (one-time) to cover up to 40 engineering hours; balance billed T&M or absorbed based on commit
   - Support: Standard (8x5) during pilot; upgrade path to Enhanced (24x7 oncall) at go-live

2) Commit (months 7-30):
   - Platform fee amortized over 24 months on the committed quantity (applies to platform fee portion only)
   - Discount schedule: tiered based on committed GPU hours; example provided in the attached spreadsheet
   - SLA uplift available with a fixed on-call retainer (we can price per region)

Key constraints: discounts and credits require a signed commitment and agreed measurement (GPU-hour or token floor). I put a placeholder deal id RBW-2083-BLK in the SOW.

I'll let Marissa and Aditya weigh in on the discount math. If this approach looks reasonable we can send a formal SOW + DocuSign link for procurement.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Accounts (Enterprise)

Subject: Fwd: Pricing sketch — suggested onramp math

Forwarding Lauren's note with suggested numbers for commercial to review. High-level thoughts:

- Onramp credit: propose a single blended credit equal to 18% of the first-year platform fees, applied as monthly credits across pilot months. That translates to ~50% effective waiver for months 1-3 and 30% for months 4-6 depending on the commit size.
- Commit discount: 10–20% off platform fee for 24-month amortization, sliding to 25% at >2x committed baseline.
- Implementation retainer: $40k cap for the pilot (covers integration + smoke tests); remainder billable unless a minimum commit is signed by month 5.

I've modeled a 12-node case in the spreadsheet — see pricing-onramp-model.xlsx. Marissa

Thanks — quick finance guardrails:

- Max allowable discount across platform fee + credits is 20% NPV at our standard cost model unless a capital contract (license up-front) is used.
- Amortization window of platform fee limited to 24 months; we cannot amortize past 24 months without additional risk approval.
- Implementation retainer can be discounted but not fully waived; recommend a 50% reduction for strategic accounts, floor $20k.
- Any SLA uplift (24x7) requires an on-call retainer priced into the SOW — don't commit to free 24x7.

Rishi
Finance, Redwood Inference

Sara — thanks for the patience while we lined up finance and commercial. Based on internal guidance the team is prepared to offer the following refined package for BlackRock's pilot -> committed path: 

Offer summary (finalized):
- Pilot (months 0-6): platform fee credit equivalent to 18% of first-year platform fees applied as monthly bill credits (approx: 100% waiver months 1-2, 40% month 3-4, 20% month 5-6 depending on actual consumption).
- Implementation retainer: $25k (applied as credit toward first invoice upon signed commitment).
- Commit (months 7-30): amortize remainder of platform fee over 24 months based on agreed committed GPU-hour floor; commit discount = 12% off the published platform fee; additional volume tiers to 20% at >2x baseline.
- Support: Standard included; Enhanced 24x7 available for an on-call retainer (we propose $8k/month regional).

Conditions: signed SOW and commitment signature by end of pilot window (month 5) to trigger credits and amortization. Procurement + legal will need the attached SOW and the pricing workbook.

Next steps: 
1) I attached the redlined SOW draft and the pricing workbook for your procurement review.
2) If procurement wants this via DocuSign we can prepare the envelope once you confirm the final billing contacts and PO process (cc'd procurement@blackrock.com).
3) If you need a tighter SLA upfront, we can price the Enhanced support retainer into month 1 and split the retainer across the amortization schedule.

Looking forward — happy to hop on a 30-min call with procurement/legal to walk through the SOW.

Regards,
